unit: Ch 8: Declaration and Payment of Dividend
note: AI-written summary of ICAI study material. Check the original for exact wording.

topics.title: Meaning, Definition, and Basics of Dividend
explain: Dividend represents the portion of profits distributed to shareholders on their investment.
Under Section 2(35), the term dividend explicitly includes any interim dividend.
The Board of Directors recommends the dividend rate, which shareholders approve at the AGM.
Shareholders can reduce or accept the recommended rate but cannot increase it beyond the Board's recommendation.
Dividend percentage is always calculated on the face value (nominal value) of shares, not market price.

flow.title: Dividend Recommendation and Approval Process
steps: Board recommends dividend rate
Board's Report mentions dividend details
AGM held with shareholders
Shareholders pass Ordinary Resolution
Dividend declared at recommended or lower rate

topics.example: If a company declares a 20% dividend on shares with face value ₹10 and market price ₹250, the dividend amount is 20% of ₹10 = ₹2 per share.
remember: Shareholders cannot declare a dividend rate higher than recommended by the Board.
Dividend calculation is based on face value, never on market price.
mistakes: Calculating dividend on the market value or purchase price of the share instead of its nominal value.

quiz.q: On which of the following values is the dividend percentage always calculated?
quiz.why: Dividend is always calculated as a percentage of the nominal or face value of a share.

quiz.q: What is the legal effect if shareholders at an AGM pass a resolution declaring a dividend rate higher than recommended by the Board?
o: Valid if passed by special resolution
Invalid as shareholders cannot exceed the Board's recommended rate
quiz.why: Under Regulation 80 of Table F, shareholders cannot declare dividend exceeding the rate recommended by the Board.

topics.title: Types of Dividend: Interim Dividend vs Final Dividend
explain: Final dividend is declared by shareholders at the AGM after audited accounts are finalized.
Interim dividend is declared by the Board of Directors between two AGMs or during the financial year.
Sources for interim dividend include P&L surplus, current year profits, or profits till the preceding quarter.
If loss is incurred in the current financial year up to the preceding quarter, interim dividend rate cannot exceed the average rate of the past 3 financial years.
Interim dividend must also be deposited in a separate bank account within 5 days of declaration.

flow.title: Interim Dividend Decision Rules
steps: Board evaluates current year financial performance
Check if loss incurred in current year
If loss, cap rate at 3-year average
Board passes resolution declaring interim dividend
Deposit funds in separate bank within 5 days

topics.example: A company incurring current-year loss declared dividends at 7%, 11%, and 12% in the last 3 years; its interim dividend cannot exceed (7+11+12)/3 = 10%.
remember: Interim dividend is declared by the Board; Final dividend is declared by Shareholders.
Current year loss caps interim dividend rate at the preceding 3-year average.
mistakes: Assuming interim dividend does not need to be deposited in a separate bank account within 5 days.

quiz.q: Who possesses the statutory authority to declare an interim dividend?
quiz.why: Under Section 123(3), interim dividend is declared directly by the Board of Directors.

quiz.q: If a company incurs a loss during the current financial year up to the preceding quarter, what is the cap on interim dividend?
o: Average rate declared during preceding 3 financial years
quiz.why: Section 123(3) restricts interim dividend during current year loss to the average rate declared in the preceding 3 financial years.

topics.title: Classification Based on Nature of Shares
explain: Preference shares enjoy preferential rights to dividend at a fixed rate prior to equity shareholders.
Cumulative preference shares accumulate unpaid arrears, which must be fully cleared before equity dividends are paid.
Non-cumulative preference dividends lapse if profits in a particular year are insufficient.
Equity dividend varies based on available distributable profits and Board recommendation.
Under Section 51, dividend can be paid in proportion to paid-up capital if authorized by the Articles.

flow.title: Priority of Dividend Payment
steps: Determine distributable profits for the year
Pay arrears on cumulative preference shares
Pay current year dividend on preference shares
Allocate remaining profit for equity dividend
Distribute equity dividend based on paid-up capital

topics.example: If a ₹10 share is ₹5 paid-up and Articles permit Section 51, a ₹5 per share dividend rate yields ₹2.50 dividend on that partly paid share.
remember: Cumulative preference arrears must be cleared before any equity dividend distribution.
Proportional dividend payment requires explicit authorization in Articles of Association.
mistakes: Paying equity dividend while cumulative preference share arrears remain unpaid.

quiz.q: What happens to unpaid dividends on cumulative preference shares during a year of profit deficiency?
o: They accumulate and are payable in future profitable years
They automatically convert to equity shares
They are paid directly out of capital
quiz.why: Cumulative preference shares accumulate unpaid dividend arrears until cleared in full in future profitable years.

quiz.q: Can a company pay dividend in proportion to the amount paid-up on each share?
o: No, dividend per share must be identical
Yes, provided it is authorized by its Articles of Association
Yes, with prior Central Government approval
No, unless all shares are fully paid-up
quiz.why: Section 51 allows proportional dividend based on paid-up capital if authorized by Articles.

topics.title: Sources for Declaration of Dividend & Depreciation Requirement
explain: Dividend can be paid out of current year profits, undistributed past profits (free reserves), or both.
Money provided by Central or State Government pursuant to a guarantee can also be used.
Providing depreciation per Schedule II is mandatory before declaring dividend out of current profits.
Carried-over past losses and unprovided depreciation must be set off against current profits first.
Unrealized gains, notional gains, and revaluation reserves cannot be used to pay dividend.

flow.title: Distributable Profit Calculation Steps
steps: Compute current year revenue profits
Deduct current year depreciation per Schedule II
Set off carried over past losses and depreciation
Exclude unrealized or revaluation gains
Arrive at net profit available for dividend

topics.example: Shreyas Mechanics Ltd gained ₹20 lakh by revaluing land; this revaluation profit cannot be used for dividend declaration as it is not a free reserve.
remember: Depreciation per Schedule II is mandatory before declaring dividend.
Past losses and past unprovided depreciation must be set off first.
mistakes: Including revaluation reserves or unrealized paper gains in free reserves available for dividend.

quiz.q: Which of the following sources CANNOT be used by a company for declaring dividend?
o: Revaluation reserves created by revaluing assets
Money provided by Government pursuant to a guarantee
quiz.why: Revaluation reserves and unrealized gains are excluded from free reserves available for dividend declaration.

quiz.q: What is mandatory before declaring dividend out of current financial year profits?
o: Providing depreciation per Schedule II and setting off past losses/depreciation
quiz.why: Section 123 requires mandatory provision for depreciation under Schedule II and set-off of carried-over losses before dividend declaration.

topics.title: Transfer to Reserves & Dividend out of Free Reserves
explain: Transferring profit to reserves before declaring dividend is voluntary and at company discretion.
If current profits are inadequate or absent, dividend can be declared out of free reserves under Rule 3.
Condition I: Rate of dividend ≤ average rate of preceding 3 financial years (skipped if no dividend declared in past 3 years).
Condition II: Total amount drawn ≤ 10% of (Paid-up Capital + Free Reserves) as per latest audited balance sheet.
Condition III: Amount drawn must first set off current year loss before paying equity dividend.
Condition IV: Residual free reserves after withdrawal must remain at least 15% of paid-up share capital.

flow.title: Rule 3 Withdrawal Test Sequence
steps: Check if current profits are inadequate or absent
Limit rate to 3-year average declared rate
Limit withdrawal to 10% of capital plus reserves
Deduct current year loss from drawn amount
Verify residual free reserves exceed required threshold

topics.example: Capricorn Ltd has capital ₹200 lakh, free reserves ₹240 lakh, current loss ₹30 lakh. Max withdrawal 10% of ₹440 lakh = ₹44 lakh. After adjusting ₹30 lakh loss, max dividend payable is ₹14 lakh.
remember: All four conditions of Rule 3 must be satisfied concurrently.
Transfer of current profits to general reserves is voluntary.
mistakes: Forgetting to deduct current year loss from the 10% drawn amount under Condition III.

quiz.q: What percentage of current profits is mandatorily required to be transferred to reserves before declaring dividend?
o: Nil (it is entirely at company discretion)
quiz.why: Under Section 123(1), transferring profit to general reserves before declaring dividend is completely voluntary.

quiz.q: Under Rule 3, what is the ceiling on total withdrawal from free reserves during profit inadequacy?
quiz.why: Rule 3 Condition II caps total withdrawal from accumulated free reserves at 10% of aggregate paid-up share capital and free reserves.

topics.title: Deposit and Payment Mode of Dividend
explain: The dividend amount (interim or final) must be deposited in a separate scheduled bank account within 5 days of declaration.
Dividend is payable only to the registered shareholder, or to their order, or to their banker.
The shareholder whose name appears in the Register of Members on the Record Date receives the dividend.
Dividend must be paid in cash, cheque, dividend warrant, or electronic mode; payment in kind is prohibited.
Capitalization of profits to issue fully paid bonus shares is permitted, but bonus shares cannot be given in lieu of dividend.

flow.title: Dividend Payment Execution Steps
steps: Declare dividend in General or Board Meeting
Open separate account in scheduled bank
Deposit total dividend within 5 days
Identify registered shareholders as on Record Date
Dispatch warrants or transfer electronically within 30 days

topics.example: Avantika Products Ltd declared dividend on 24th September 2026; the total dividend must be deposited in a separate bank account by 29th September 2026.
remember: Deposit dividend in a separate bank account within 5 days of declaration.
Only the registered owner on the Record Date is entitled to receive dividend.
mistakes: Believing that dividend can be paid in kind using company products or merchandise.

quiz.q: Within how many days from dividend declaration must the total dividend amount be deposited in a separate bank account?
quiz.why: Section 123(4) mandates depositing declared dividend in a separate scheduled bank account within 5 days.

quiz.q: Can a company issue bonus shares to shareholders in lieu of cash dividend?
o: Yes, if passed by special resolution
No, bonus shares cannot be issued in lieu of dividend
quiz.why: First proviso to Section 123(5) specifies that bonus shares cannot be issued in lieu of dividend.

topics.title: Prohibition on Declaration of Dividend
explain: Section 123(6) prohibits equity dividend declaration if a company defaults under Section 73 or 74 (deposit acceptance and repayment).
This prohibition remains active as long as the default in deposit repayment continues.
Section 8 companies (charitable objects) are strictly prohibited from paying any dividend to their members under Section 8(1).
Profits of Section 8 companies must be applied exclusively towards promoting their organizational objects.

flow.title: Dividend Prohibition Verification Steps
steps: Check if the entity is Section 8 company
If Section 8, dividend is prohibited
Check deposit default under Section 73 or 74
If deposit default exists, dividend is prohibited
If fully compliant, proceed to declare dividend

topics.example: ABC Tractors Ltd defaulted in repaying public deposits accepted under Section 74; it cannot declare any equity dividend while the failure persists.
remember: Section 8 companies can never declare dividends under any circumstances.
Default in deposit repayment under Section 73/74 completely blocks equity dividend.
mistakes: Assuming a Section 8 company can distribute dividend if approved unanimously by shareholders.

quiz.q: Which type of company is strictly prohibited from distributing dividends to its members?
quiz.why: Section 8(1) strictly prohibits charitable companies from paying dividends to their members.

quiz.q: XYZ Ltd defaulted on public deposit repayments under Section 74. Can it declare dividend on equity shares?
o: No, dividend declaration is prohibited while default continues
quiz.why: Section 123(6) prohibits equity dividend declaration so long as failure to comply with Section 73 or 74 continues.

topics.title: Unpaid Dividend Account (UDA)
explain: Unpaid or unclaimed dividend within 30 days of declaration must be transferred to Unpaid Dividend Account (UDA) within 7 days.
UDA is a special account opened by the company in any scheduled bank.
Within 90 days of UDA transfer, the company must publish a statement of names, addresses, and unpaid amounts on its website.
Failure to transfer funds to UDA attracts simple interest @ 12% p.a. payable to affected members.
Funds remaining in UDA for 7 consecutive years (along with underlying shares) must be transferred to IEPF.

flow.title: Unpaid Dividend Processing Timeline
steps: Day 0: Dividend declared
Day 1 to 30: Payment window
Day 31 to 37: Transfer unpaid funds to UDA
Within 90 days: Upload statement on website
After 7 years: Transfer funds to IEPF

topics.example: Dividend declared on 1st May remains unpaid to the extent of ₹50,000 on 31st May; company must transfer ₹50,000 to UDA by 7th June.
remember: Transfer to UDA: Within 7 days after expiry of 30 days from declaration.
Default interest for late UDA transfer: 12% p.a.
Transfer to IEPF: After 7 years in UDA.
mistakes: Calculating the 7-day UDA transfer limit from the date of declaration rather than from the end of the 30-day payment period.

quiz.q: Within how many days from the expiry of the 30-day dividend payment period must unpaid dividend be transferred to UDA?
quiz.why: Section 124(1) requires transfer to UDA within 7 days after the expiry of the 30-day period from declaration.

quiz.q: What interest rate applies if a company defaults in transferring unpaid dividend to the UDA?
quiz.why: Section 124(3) imposes interest @ 12% p.a. on amounts not transferred to UDA on time.

topics.title: Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF)
explain: IEPF is established by Central Government to promote investor awareness and protect investor interests.
Sources credited to IEPF include UDA funds unpaid for 7 years, matured deposits/debentures unpaid for 7 years, grants, and disgorged amounts.
Fund is utilized for refunding unclaimed dividends/deposits, investor education, and reimbursing legal expenses for class action suits (Sections 37/245).
Secretary, MCA is the ex-officio Chairperson of IEPF Authority, accompanied by up to 7 members and a CEO.
Accounts of IEPF are audited annually by the CAG and laid before both Houses of Parliament.

flow.title: IEPF Administration and Reporting Structure
steps: Unclaimed funds credited to IEPF after 7 years
IEPF Authority administers and maintains accounts
CAG conducts annual audit of IEPF accounts
Authority submits annual report to Central Government
Reports laid before both Houses of Parliament

topics.example: Matured debentures unpaid for 7 years are transferred to IEPF; the investor can later submit a claim to the IEPF Authority to get a refund.
remember: Retention period in UDA before transfer to IEPF is 7 years.
IEPF funds can reimburse legal fees incurred by investors in class action suits.
mistakes: Assuming funds transferred to IEPF can never be reclaimed by the original investor.

quiz.q: Which of the following items is credited to the Investor Education and Protection Fund (IEPF)?
o: Unpaid dividend in UDA after 1 year
Matured deposits remaining unpaid for 7 years from due date
quiz.why: Section 125(2) mandates crediting matured deposits remaining unclaimed/unpaid for 7 years to IEPF.

quiz.q: Who acts as the ex-officio Chairperson of the IEPF Authority?
quiz.why: Under IEPF Rules 2016, Secretary, Ministry of Corporate Affairs is the ex-officio Chairperson of IEPF Authority.

topics.title: Right of Dividend, Rights Shares, and Bonus Shares in Abeyance
explain: When share transfer instruments are delivered to a company but pending registration, rights are kept in abeyance.
Dividend on such pending shares must be transferred to the Unpaid Dividend Account (UDA).
Exception: Dividend can be paid directly to transferee if authorized in writing by the registered transferor.
Rights share offers under Section 62(1)(a) must be kept in abeyance.
Issue of fully paid bonus shares must also be kept in abeyance pending transfer registration.

flow.title: Abeyance Mechanism Pending Transfer Registration
steps: Shareholder delivers transfer instrument to company
Transfer registration pending with company
Dividend directed to UDA unless written authority given
Rights share offer under Section 62 kept in abeyance
Bonus shares issue kept in abeyance

topics.example: Mr. A sells shares to Mr. B. Pending transfer registration by the company, declared dividends go to UDA unless Mr. A authorizes payment to Mr. B in writing.
remember: Dividend goes to UDA unless written authorization is provided by registered transferor.
Both rights shares and bonus shares are strictly held in abeyance.
mistakes: Issuing bonus shares directly to the transferee before transfer registration is formally completed.

quiz.q: Where must dividend be directed when share transfer registration is pending with the company?
o: Transferred to Unpaid Dividend Account unless written authorization given by registered holder
quiz.why: Section 126(a) mandates transferring dividend to UDA unless registered holder authorizes payment to transferee in writing.

quiz.q: What happens to bonus shares issued while share transfer registration is pending?
o: They are sold at public auction
quiz.why: Section 126(b) specifies that any issue of fully paid bonus shares must be kept in abeyance pending transfer registration.

topics.title: Punishment for Failure to Distribute Dividend & Exemptions
explain: Dividend must be paid or warrants posted within 30 days from the date of declaration.
Failure to post warrants within 30 days renders every default director punishable with imprisonment up to 2 years and fine min ₹1,000 per day.
Company is liable to pay simple interest @ 18% p.a. for the default duration.
Exemption applies if dividend could not be paid due to operation of law, dispute, direction non-compliance communicated, or lawful set-off.
Dividends can be lawfully adjusted against calls in arrears or other sums due from the shareholder.
Nidhi Companies: For dividend ≤ ₹100, local newspaper publication and 3-month notice board display is valid compliance.

flow.title: Section 127 Enforcement and Exemption Test
steps: Dividend declared by company
Post warrant or credit account within 30 days
If defaulted, check 5 statutory exemptions
If exempted, no offence or penalty applies
If not exempted, director penalty and interest apply

topics.example: Mr. Alok owes ₹80,000 call money; company adjusts his declared ₹80,000 dividend against unpaid calls. This is valid under Section 127 proviso (d) with no penalty.
remember: Posting dividend warrants within 30 days absolves the company from penalty regardless of postal delay.
Penal interest rate on company for default is 18% p.a.
Dividend can be legally adjusted against call arrears.
mistakes: Holding company liable under Section 127 when dividend warrant was posted within 30 days but delayed in postal transit.

quiz.q: What rate of simple interest is a company liable to pay under Section 127 for failing to distribute dividend within 30 days?
quiz.why: Section 127 mandates simple interest at 18% p.a. during default period for failure to distribute dividend within 30 days.

quiz.q: In which case is a company EXEMPT from punishment under Section 127 for non-payment of dividend within 30 days?
o: Cash flow shortage in bank account
Dividend lawfully adjusted against call money due from shareholder
Directors were occupied with annual audit
quiz.why: Section 127 proviso (d) explicitly exempts company where dividend is lawfully adjusted against any sum due from the shareholder.
